review.why: The PR removes the 404 response when a user does not exist, changing the behavior from returning a 404 error to returning an empty list with 200 OK for non-existent user IDs.

suspicions.claim: The @other_responses({404: 'User not found'}) decorator remains on the endpoint but the 404 is never raised, so API documentation incorrectly advertises a 404 response.
suspicions.trigger: Inspect the generated API documentation (e.g., /docs) for the endpoint GET /api/users/<id>/posts and observe that a 404 response is documented even though the implementation cannot produce it.
suspicions.evidence: Probe round2 probe_s2_docs_404_check fetched /docs but the response bodies are truncated HTML, so presence of a documented 404 for the endpoint cannot be verified.

suspicions.claim: If the database contains posts with a user_id that references a non-existent user (orphaned posts), the new query will return those posts while the old code would have aborted with 404 before reaching the relationship.
suspicions.trigger: Directly insert a Post row with user_id=999999 (a user that does not exist) into the database. Then send GET /api/users/999999/posts with a valid Authorization header. Read back the response body; it will contain the orphaned post(s) instead of 404.
suspicions.evidence: Probe probe_s3 sent GET /api/users/999999/posts without first inserting an orphaned post with user_id=999999, so the triggering condition was not met.
